second_method.method: printed BLUE PRINT difficulty table total (Easy 10 + Average 5 + Difficulty 5 = 20), pdf 78; independently, the answer side's keys counted

count_gate.note: Question side labels 1-20 monotonic, no gaps, no duplicates (I 1-5, II 6-10, III 11-15, IV 16, V 17-18, VI 19, 20); q16 items A-G, q19 sub-questions A-F and q20 sub-questions 1-4 are parts of their questions. Answer side keys 1-20 in order (pdf 122-123). BLUE PRINT 10/5/5 = 20 = audited count. Difficulty per question: easy 0, average 0, difficult 0, untagged 20.

method_notes: Pages: Q pdf 78 (heading, LO 11, BLUE PRINT, q1-5) 79 (q6-14) 80 (q14 options-q18) 81 (q19 passage + A-F) 82 (q20 picture + 1-4). A side 'Sample answers 20' pdf 122 (keys 1-13), pdf 123 (14-20). Folios = pdf page.

ANSWER SIDE (analysed first): keys 1-16 answer q1-q16 by number. Keys 17 and 18 answer other questions (17 fits q12, 18 fits q19 B) -> q17, q18 empty + 'key belongs to another paper version'. Key 19 answers q19's sub-question E only and key 20 answers q20's sub-question 2 only -> stored with 'answer truncated in source'.

Sections: s1 I fill q1-5; s2 II match q6-10 (numbered rows -> one-pair match questions); s3 III mcq q11-15 (three options A-C; keys print text only -> addendum §4.2 matching: q14 'Education' -> B by pass 1; q11 'He wakes up early.', q12 'VegetablesTo sell', q13 'Plays with a friend.', q15 'ToothMust be rubbed' match no option -> null + 'key text not among options' with the suggested letter); s4 IV q16 ordering (items A-G in the stem; key = six re-worded lines, stored as the sequence verbatim + 'key text does not address question'); s5 V q17-18; s6 VI q19 (passage stimulus); s7 q20 (picture stimulus).
MARKS (R-E9, rev 3): s2 '5X1=5' -> 1; s3 '5X1=5' -> 1; null: s1 '5X1=6' (arithmetic wrong), s4 '7X1=7' over 1 q, s5 '[Marks: 4 × 2 = 8]' over 2 q, s6 '6X1=6' over 1 q, s7 '4*1=4' over 1 q.
DIFFICULTY: none printed -> null + 'no difficulty tag'. quota_table difficulty_only; second method = BLUE PRINT total 20 (agrees). LO (R-E10): lesson LO 11, lo_source 'lesson_table'.
FIGURES (v1.4 §14.10): q20's three-panel picture (pdf 82, one embedded image) -> stimulus crop.

Source wording kept: key 5 'Claim' (right), q13 option A 'He watches the distance vision.', glued words in keys ('VegetablesTo sell', 'ToothMust be rubbed', 'EveningPlays'); key 18 'Wit hout school …' quoted verbatim in q18's flag.

stimuli.text: The children who are engaged in work for money at an early age are called child labourers. They do not get access to school, learning and play. They miss proper education. Many works are dangerous for children. They getting into health risks is more. They get into hazards quickly. May be punished by the owners. There are possibilities of getting into bad habits. So the Government has enforced the child labour Prohibition Act. Children of school age are being identified and brought back to school. Efforts are made to provide education to these children.

questions.text:
Read the passage below and answer the questions given.
A. Who are child labourers?
B. What they are going to miss in life?
C. Is it safe to work in small age, in dangerous places? How it is dangerous?
D. Who may punish these children?
E. Which is the act enforced by Government to save these children?
F. What is the good effort by the government towards these children?
questions.section_signal: VI. 19. Read the passage below and answer the questions given.

answer.value:
A. Children who are engaged in work at an early age are child labourers.
B. They miss school, learning and playing — they miss proper education.
C. No. Many jobs are dangerous for children; they are open to health risks.
D. They may be punished by the owners.
E. The Child Labour Prohibition Act.
F. Children of school age are identified and brought back to school, and efforts are made to give them good education.
